note: Compared with Cook's final ratings and the last public polls. Uncalled races can still shift as more votes are counted.

items.title: No tracked race called for a Republican
items.text: Of the 72 races on this page, 43 have been projected and all 43 went to Democrats, including 30 seats that flip from Republican control. The rest are still uncalled.

items.title: Texas flips both top races
items.text: AP projected Talarico (D) over Paxton (R) for Senate, 59.2%–39.2%, well above final polls (Talarico +3 to +7). AP also projected Hinojosa (D) over Gov. Abbott (R), after a final poll showing a 1-point race.

items.title: Senate toss-ups break one way
items.text: Democrats were projected to win the Maine, Ohio, Kansas and Iowa Senate races, all rated toss-ups by Cook. Sen. Collins conceded in Maine.

items.title: Michigan was the closest Senate call
items.text: Fox News and Decision Desk HQ projected El-Sayed (D) over Rogers (R), who led 49.5%–48.5% with about 44% counted, far tighter than the 11-point final NYT/Siena poll. AP had not called it.

items.title: NY-21 is the reversal of the night
items.text: Gendebien (D) led early, but with about 99% counted Constantino (R) leads 49%–47%, per WAMC. No desk call yet.

items.title: Close House races still out
items.text: FL-27 (Salazar up under 1 point with 99% counted), ME-02 (likely headed to ranked-choice tabulation), MI-04, MI-07 and CO-04 remain uncalled. Kansas governor is 50.3%–49.7%.
